Iron and Steel Technology Roadmap                 Glossary
Towards more sustainable steelmaking

Glossary

Apparent steel use         Crude steel production plus imports less exports of both
                           crude steel and intermediate steel products; steel use by next-
Basic oxygen furnace       tier manufacturers, such as vehicle makers, fabricators and
Best available technology  construction companies.
Blast furnace              A steelmaking furnace that produces steel from molten iron,
Carbon steel               often in conjunction with some scrap, by reducing the carbon
Clinker                    content of the mixture with the aid of pure oxygen.
                           Technology designs and configurations that enable the lowest
Coke                       energy intensities practically achievable for a given process
Coke oven                  unit with commercial technology.
Coking coal                The main process unit used globally for the production of iron
                           from iron ore.
Crude steel                A collective term for steel where the main alloying element is
Direct emissions           carbon.
                           The main active ingredient in Portland cement. Cement is
Direct reduced iron        typically composed of < 100% clinker, with clinker substitutes,
DRI furnace                including blast furnace slag sourced from the steel industry,
Electric arc furnace       used to make up the remainder.
                           Carbonised coal used in the blast furnace to chemically
                           reduce iron ore.                                                  IEA. All rights reserved.
                           An industrial oven for producing coke from coking coal.
                           Coal with a quality that allows the production of a coke
                           suitable to support a blast furnace charge. It is a type of hard
                           coal and has a gross calorific value greater than 23 865 kJ/kg
                           (5 700 kcal/kg) on an ash-free but moist basis.
                           Steel as it emerges in its first solid state, before rolling and
                           other finishing processes.
                           CO2 emissions that are directly attributable to the iron and
                           steel sector as defined in this publication, including direct
                           process emissions (e.g. from the production and use of lime
                           fluxes) and energy-related emissions (e.g. from the
                           combustion of coal). See Box 1.3 for further details.
                           Iron produced from iron ore pellets in a DRI furnace.
                           An alternative process to the blast furnace for making iron
                           from iron ore in the solid phase.
                           An electric furnace for making steel from scrap and/or DRI by
                           melting it with an electric arc. Oxygen and other elements are
                           introduced to adjust the final composition of the steel.

                                      PAGE | 184
Iron and Steel Technology Roadmap                 Glossary
Towards more sustainable steelmaking

Electric furnace          A furnace grouping including electric arc furnaces and             IEA. All rights reserved.
Electrolyser              induction furnaces, both of which are powered using
End-of-life scrap         electricity.
End-use demand            An electrochemical process unit for producing hydrogen from
                          water using electricity.
Finished steel            Scrap steel generated at the end of a steel-containing
                          product's lifetime. Synonyms include old scrap, post-
Home scrap                consumer scrap and obsolete scrap.
                          The quantity of steel that makes its way into end-use products
Hot metal                 (buildings, vehicles, machinery, etc.), excluding the quantities
Hydrogen-based DRI        that become scrap during semi-manufacturing and
                          manufacturing (home scrap and prompt scrap). As such, total
Indirect emissions        end-use demand is lower than total production.
Induction furnace         Steel products in their final finished form, ready to be used in
Innovative blast furnace  the manufacture of steel-containing goods. Key examples of
Innovative smelting       finished steel products include coil, sheets, strips, wire, bars,
reduction                 rods, tubes, pipes, rail and plated/coated versions of each of
In-use stocks             these products.
Iron ore                  Scrap steel generated due to the imperfect yields of
                          steelmaking, rolling and finishing processes within a site.
                          Synonyms include return scrap, internal scrap and semi-
                          manufacturing scrap.
                          Molten iron produced in the blast furnace or smelting
                          reduction furnace.
                          An alternative DRI process currently under development to
                          produce sponge iron from pellets using hydrogen as the
                          reduction agent instead of a mixture of hydrogen and carbon
                          monoxide as in a regular DRI furnace.
                          CO2 emissions from the generation of electricity and imported
                          heat that are consumed in the iron and steel sector.
                          An electric furnace that utilises electromagnetic induction to
                          make steel from scrap (sometimes iron is also used).
                          A class of retrofit and new-build processes currently under
                          development to adapt commercial blast furnace designs to
                          make them more amenable to CO2 capture.
                          An alternative class of smelting reduction process currently
                          under development that reduces energy consumption and
                          produces a concentrated stream of CO2 that is more amenable
                          to capture.
                          The amount of iron and steel contained in end-use products
                          (buildings, vehicles, machinery, etc.) in use in society at a
                          given point in time.
                          The primary virgin raw material input to steelmaking.

                                      PAGE | 185
Iron and Steel Technology Roadmap     Glossary
Towards more sustainable steelmaking

Lime fluxes           Limestone and dolomite, either used directly or after              IEA. All rights reserved.
                      processing (e.g. into lime) that help remove impurities such as
Lump ore              sulphur, phosphorus and silica in the ironmaking and
Metallic inputs       steelmaking processes.
Open hearth furnace   A type of iron ore that is already of the correct size and
Pellets               concentration to be added to the ironmaking process directly,
Pig iron              without intermediate upgrading processes.
Primary production    The combined total of scrap and iron inputs to a steelmaking
Prompt scrap          furnace.
                      A largely superseded furnace design for producing steel from
Rolling processes     iron and often some scrap.
                      An enriched form of iron ore used as an input to DRI furnaces
Scrap                 and blast furnaces.
Secondary production  A solid form of iron with a high carbon content produced from
Semi-finished steel   iron ore in a blast furnace or smelting reduction process.
Sinter                Steel production that uses iron ore as its primary source of
                      metallic input.
Slag                  Scrap steel generated during the manufacture of steel
Smelting              products by first-tier customers, such as vehicle makers.
Smelting reduction    Synonyms include new scrap, industrial scrap and
Sponge iron           manufacturing scrap.
                      After steel is cast, it makes its way through a variety of semi-
                      finishing and finishing processes to adjust its size and material
                      properties. Rolling is a key process among these, and can be
                      carried out hot or cold.
                      A collective name for home scrap, prompt scrap and end-of-
                      life scrap.
                      Electric furnace production that is primarily fed by scrap, as
                      opposed to pig iron or sponge iron.
                      Steel after it proceeds through its first round of finishing
                      processes, such as rolling. The main examples of semi-finished
                      steel products are blooms and billets.
                      An upgraded form of iron ore used mainly in blast furnaces.
                      Iron ore fines are mixed with limestone and coke breeze, and
                      then heated to form clumps that are more suitable for use in
                      the blast furnace.
                      A co-product generated in blast furnaces and other
                      ironmaking and steelmaking process units.
                      A general term for the extraction of a metal from its ore using
                      heat.
                      A commercial class of ironmaking processes that form an
                      alternative to using a blast furnace and a coke oven.
                      Iron produced in a direct reduced iron furnace in the solid
                      phase.

Iron and Steel Technology Roadmap                 Glossary
Towards more sustainable steelmaking

Steel off-gases             Co-product gases with significant energy content that are
Technology readiness level  generated in various process units, most notably coke oven
                            gas and blast furnace gas.
True steel use
Torrefaction                A scale used to assess where a technology is on its journey
                            from initial idea to maturity; the IEA uses a scale with 11
                            increments which are grouped into six categories: Concept
                            (TRL 1-3), Small prototype (TRL 4), Large prototype (TRL 5-6),
                            Demonstration (TRL 7-8), Early adoption (TRL 9-10) and Mature
                            (TRL 11). See Box 2.5 for further details.

                            In addition to apparent steel use, this metric incorporates to
                            some degree the indirect trade of steel in steel-containing
                            products with the aim of better-representing steel use by final
                            consumers.

                            A pyrolytic process used to upgrade the properties of biomass
                            to make it suitable for use in several steelmaking processes.
